items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: the producer of the show, his name was Earl Dancer, the husband of Ethel Waters.

ctx.x: It was a frameup. And we went to Cleveland, opened at the Club Plantation there, and we had become used to playing shows by that time, and they brought in a black show from New York City, a first class black show, brought Seamstress in, and chorus girls, had principals, and the producer of the show, his name was Earl Dancer, the husband of Ethel Waters.

And the show opened with a bang. We played dinner engagements and nightclub engagements, we used to work from 6:00 to 8:00, from 10:00 to 2:00. The band was a riot, the show was great. We played right on through 1929 into 1930. Two weeks after 1930, business started falling off. You know the crash came in 1929, and so it was gradually, the times were catching up with the crash. So in about another week and a half I used to go to work by streetcar, because streetcar would put me off a block from where I worked and…
